nodes.name: NiCo-LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of commercial Ni foam (3×4 cm²) was cleaned by ultrasonication with ethanol and deionized water for 15 min, respectively, and the substrate was then transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave (40 ml) containing a homogenous solution of 36 ml deionized water, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.5 mmol), Co(NO3)2·6H2O (0.5 mmol), NH4F (4 mmol) and urea (CH4N2O, 5 mmol). Afterwards, the autoclave was sealed and maintained at 100 °C for 8 h. After reaction, the sample was taken out and washed three times with deionized water and ethanol, respectively, and dried at 60 °C for 10 h under vacuum.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiCo–LDH ... dried at 60 °C for 10 h under vacuum.

nodes.name: NiCoP phosphorization
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g of NaH2PO2·H2O was placed upstream in a quartz tube to serve as the phosphorous source, whereas the obtained NiCo–LDH was placed at the centre of the quartz tube and then the quartz tube was heated at 300 °C for 2 h with a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹ in Ar atmosphere. After reaction, the furnace was turned off and naturally cooled to room temperature under Ar atmosphere to obtain NiCoP.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiCoP ... naturally cooled to room temperature under Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: NiCoP-Cr2O3 electrodeposition and calcination
nodes.procedure: Chromium hydroxide was electrodeposited onto NiCoP using a two-electrode system, with NiCoP as the working electrode (1 cm²) and a stainless-steel mesh as the counter electrode, and the electrolyte solution contained 6 mmol L⁻¹ Cr(NO3)3·9H2O. The electrodeposition current was set as -10 mA cm⁻², with deposition time ranging from 10 to 1,800 s. After electrodeposition, the electrode was placed in a quartz tube, which was heated at 300 °C for 2 h in a tube furnace under Ar atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiCoP–Cr2O3 ... heated at 300 °C for 2 h in a tube furnace under Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: NiCoFe hydroxide hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of commercial Ni foam (3×4 cm²) was cleaned by ultrasonication with ethanol and deionized water for 15 min, respectively, and the substrate was then transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave (40 ml) containing a homogenous solution of 36 ml deionized water, Co(NO3)2·6H2O (3 mmol), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (1 mmol), NH4F (4 mmol) and urea (CH4N2O, 5 mmol). Afterwards, the autoclave was sealed and maintained at 120 °C for 6 h. After reaction, the sample was taken out and washed three times with deionized water and ethanol, respectively, and dried at 60 °C for 10 h under vacuum.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiCoFeP First, NiCoFe hydroxide was synthesized ... dried at 60 °C for 10 h under vacuum.

nodes.name: NiCoFeP phosphorization
nodes.procedure: 0.5 g of NaH2PO2·H2O was placed upstream in a quartz tube to serve as the phosphorous source, whereas the obtained NiCoFe hydroxide was placed at the centre of the quartz tube and then the quartz tube was heated at 300 °C for 2 h with a heating rate of 2 °C min⁻¹ in Ar atmosphere. After reaction, the furnace was turned off and naturally cooled to room temperature under Ar atmosphere to obtain NiCoFeP.
nodes.source_text: NiCoFeP was synthesized by phosphorization ... naturally cooled to room temperature under Ar atmosphere.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A piece of commercial Ni foam (3×4 cm²) was cleaned by ultrasonication with ethanol and deionized water for 15 min, respectively, and the substrate was then transferred to a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave (40 ml) containing a homogenous solution of 36 ml deionized water, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.66 mmol), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (0.33 mmol), NH4F (4 mmol) and urea (CH4N2O, 5 mmol). Afterwards, the autoclave was sealed and maintained at 120 °C for 6 h. After reaction, the sample was taken out and washed three times with deionized water and ethanol, respectively, and dried at 60 °C for 10 h under vacuum.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of NiFeP NiFeP was synthesized by the same method as for NiCoFeP but using Ni(NO3)2·6H2O (0.66 mmol), Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (0.33 mmol) and urea (CH4N2O, 5 mmol) to prepare NiFe–LDH.

nodes.name: NiFeP phosphorization
nodes.procedure: Same phosphorization method as NiCoFeP using 0.5 g NaH2PO2·H2O upstream, NiFe–LDH at center, heated at 300 °C for 2 h, 2 °C/min ramp in Ar, natural cool.
nodes.source_text: NiFeP was synthesized by the same method as for NiCoFeP...

nodes.name: Ni/NiO/Cr2O3 electrodeposition and calcination
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition solution: 5 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O + 0.6 mmol Cr(NO3)3·9H2O in 150 ml water. Ni foam (2×3 cm²) cleaned by ultrasonication ethanol/DI water 15 min. Three-electrode system: Ni foam working electrode, stainless-steel mesh counter, SCE reference. Electrodeposition at -1.2 V until 50 C cm⁻² charge. Washed 3x DI water/ethanol, dried 60 °C 10 h vacuum. Then calcined at 300 °C 1 h under 5% H2 atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Ni/NiO/Cr2O3 ... heated at 300 °C for 1 h under 5% H2 atmosphere.

nodes.description: Intermittent stability at 0.5 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater with 12-h cycles
nodes.source_text: The full water electrolysis cell with a NiCoP–Cr₂O₃ cathode and a NiCoFeP anode could stably operate at a current density of 0.5 A cm⁻² for 10,000 h in 1 M NaOH + seawater with 12-h start–shutdown intervals. The activity decay rate was as low as 0.5% khr⁻¹ (Fig. 2d).

nodes.description: Intermittent stability at 1 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater with 10-min cycles
nodes.source_text: The results showed that NiCoP–·Cr₂O₃ could maintain stable operation at a current density of 1 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater with 10-min start–shutdown cycles for 4,500 h (Fig. 2e).

nodes.description: Intermittent stability at 10 A cm⁻² in 20 wt% NaOH + seawater with 12-h cycles
nodes.source_text: Furthermore, the NiCoP–Cr₂O₃ catalyst exhibits stable operation under a harsher condition at 10 A cm⁻² for 700 h with a small voltage increase of less than 1.8% khr⁻¹.

nodes.description: AEM electrolyser intermittent stability at 1 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: h, Intermittent stability test of an AEM electrolyser (with NiCoP–·Cr₂O₃ cathode and NiFeP anode) recorded at 1 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater with 12-h start and 6-h shutdown cycles at 60 °C.

nodes.description: Intermittent stability comparison at 0.5 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: By contrast, the NiCo–LDH cathode showed poor resistance to start–shutdown fluctuations with 20.58% activity decay in 800 h of intermittent electrolysis at 0.5 A cm⁻² in 1 M NaOH + seawater.

nodes.description: Three-electrode HER evaluation in alkaline electrolyte
nodes.source_text: We used a standard three-electrode system to evaluate the hydrogen evolution performance of NiCoP–·Cr₂O₃ cathode. ... The polarization curves, Tafel plots and intermittent stability test results indicated that NiCoP–·Cr₂O₃ exhibited excellent hydrogen evolution activity and anti-fluctuation stability in 1 M NaOH.

nodes.description: AEM electrolyser performance at various current densities
nodes.source_text: an alkaline anion exchange membrane (AEM) electrolyser equipped with NiCoP–Cr₂O₃ cathode and NiFe–LDH anode was assembled ... which achieved 1 and 4 A cm⁻² (1 M KOH, 80 °C) with a cell voltage of only 1.74 and 1.99 V, respectively.

nodes.description: Intermittent stability at 3 A cm⁻² in 20 wt% NaOH + seawater
nodes.source_text: Even at very high operating current densities (for example, 3-10 A cm⁻², the NiCoP–·Cr₂O₃ cathode showed long time stable performance in 20 wt% NaOH + seawater (Fig. 2f,g).

nodes.evidence_snippet: Inset, SEM image of NiCoP– · Cr₂O₃. Scale bar, 200 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS after HER shows regular distribution of Co, P, Ni elements except Cr₂O₃ coating on surface and partially oxidized PO₄⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TOF-SIMS spectra recorded immediately after HER (Fig. 3a–d and Supplementary Fig. 38) revealed a regular distribution of elements within NiCoP– · Cr₂O₃ except for the Cr₂O₃ coating on the surface and partially oxidized PO₄⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: TOF-SIMS after 24 h shutdown shows elemental segregation with Co and CoO stratified distribution, opposite P distribution, and Ni accumulation in inner layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, after 24 h of shutdown time, elemental segregation occurred (Fig. 3e–h and Supplementary Fig. 39).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ar⁺ XPS of Co species shows marked increase in oxidation state after shutdown (65.15% Co³⁺, 34.85% Co²⁺ surface; interior divalent); Ni⁰ proportion increases to 15.37% at 100.79 s sputtering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ar⁺ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurement further confirmed the electronic structure change of NiCoP– · Cr₂O₃ under intermittent electrolysis conditions (Supplementary Figs. 40 and 41), revealing a marked increase in the oxidation state of Co after shutdown (Fig. 3i,j).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows P–O and phosphate ion vibrations under OCV that disappear under cathodic potential and re-emerge after shutdown, indicating dynamic phosphate layer recovery.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Operando Raman spectroscopy measurements were conducted to monitor the surface structure change under start–shutdown conditions (Fig. 3m).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM after HER shows regular NiCoP lattice; after shutdown reveals passivation layers of CoO/Cr₂O₃ outermost, amorphous phosphates, cubic CoO lattice, and inner NiCoP lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We used high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) to analyse the composition of NiCoP– · Cr₂O₃ in two distinct states (Fig. 4a).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS confirms Co oxidation from NiCoP to CoO phase after shutdown; no shifts in Ni L-edge, Co L-edge, P K-edge after cycles compared to post-HER state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) and atomic elemental mapping (Fig. 4b,d and Supplementary Fig. 48) indicate that it shares the same atomic structure as the hexagonal NiCoP.

visual_evidence.name: Pseudo in situ EELS O K-edge

nodes.characterization_summary: X-ray powder diffraction patterns recorded in 10° to 90° range.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray powder diffraction patterns were recorded on an X-ray diffractometer (Rigaku D/Max 2500) in the diffraction angle range from 10° to 90° at a scan rate of 5° min⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: IC measurement shows phosphate ion content <10 ppb (below detection limit) after 120 h.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The result showed that the phosphate ion content was less than 10 ppb (Fig. 3o), lower than the detection limit.
